primaryText: Ik-ken-no mise-ga hiraite-ita node, hairu koto-ni shita.
translation: Since one shop was open, (I) decided to go in.
comment: The second criterion of the definition: a true classifier readily co-occurs with a noun denoting the enumerated referent.

primaryText: mik-ka tatte
translation: three days later
comment: An unclassified time word: adding the co-referring noun hi 'day' is grammatical but marked, so -ka is not a classifier by the second criterion.

primaryText: Ni-rooru-o sono hikidashi-ni irete kudasai.
translation: Please put two rolls in that drawer.
comment: The classifier rooru cannot appear without an accompanying noun or antecedent.

primaryText: Ashi-no ura-to kutsu-no aida-ni hito-tsubu-mo hairu-to aruku koto-ga kurushiku naru.
translation: If even one little piece gets between the sole of your foot and your shoe, it's painful to walk.
comment: The shape classifier tsubu does not readily stand alone without a nominal antecedent. The page prints the mark ?*.

primaryText: Kono ori-no naka-ni hebi-ga san-biki mieru.
translation: You can see three snakes in this cage.

alternatives.form: Kono ori-no naka-ni hebi-ga san-bon mieru.
Kono ori-no naka-ni hebi-ga mi-suji mieru.

comment: Animate referents are invariably marked as such: live snakes take hiki and never the shape classifiers hon or suji, though they are long and thin.

primaryText: Dewa, ringo san-ko-to banana ni-hon-de-wa doo ka, to iu to, ichi-nensei-wa magotsuku. Zenbu-de itsu-tsu da.
translation: Well, if we ask 'How about three apples and two bananas?' the first grader will be confused. All together, it's five...
comment: Shape classifiers may be replaced by the general tsu to combine referents of different classes.

primaryText: Boku-wa inu-to futari-de sanpo shi-nagara ...
translation: While I was taking a walk with my dog, ...
comment: The human classifier, unlike the shape classifiers, cannot be generalised to cover a dog together with a person; speakers vary. The page marks (5a) with %: the same sentence, (14) of Chapter 3, is one some speakers accept and most find somewhat unnatural.

primaryText: denwa ichi-dai
translation: one telephone
comment: A kind-classifier disambiguates a noun: dai picks out the telephone as apparatus and tsuu the telephone call.

primaryText: budoo hito-tsubu
translation: one grape
comment: Quality-classifiers disambiguate too: tsubu a grape, ko a grape or a bunch, fusa a bunch.

primaryText: ume ip-pon
translation: one plum branch
comment: hon a plum branch, ko a plum, and the kind-classifier rin a plum blossom.

primaryText: Hoosu-no saki-o yubi-de tsubusu-to, mizu-wa ni-hon-no kiri-ni natte ...
translation: When he squeezed the end of the hose with his fingers, the water became two streams of mist, ...
comment: A quality-classifier imposes on mist, a noun that normally takes no classifier, a shape the noun does not imply.

primaryText: mottomo igi aru kichoona nihon-no yuubin-kitte go-jut-ten-o hajimete gin-de saigen-shita shinseina fukusei-no korekushon
translation: the first collection of genuine silver reproductions of fifty of the most valuable and significant postage stamps of Japan
comment: Stamps, which normally take mai, are counted with ten, the classifier for works of art, to convey their artistic value.

primaryText: ashi yon-mai
translation: four feet
comment: Feet printed on a sheet of paper take mai rather than hon or tsu: a shape classifier marks a referent as a non-standard member of the noun's category, a use closed to the kind-classifiers.

primaryText: Ni-wa-no hoo desu.
translation: It's the birds.
context: Speaker A, offering a choice between two birds and two turtles: Hoshii-no-wa dochira desu ka? 'Which is it that you want?'
comment: A numeral-classifier pair does not answer a question about the nature of a referent; a full noun does, (8). Classifiers acknowledge category membership rather than assert it.

primaryText: kitte ichi-shiito
translation: one sheet of (postage) stamps
comment: The classifier carries an independent semantic load when one noun admits several classifiers: a sheet of stamps against one stamp.

primaryText: Ip-piki desu.
translation: One.
context: A, continuing a conversation about goldfish: Nan-biki-gurai katte-iru no? 'How many are you raising?'
comment: A noun-less numeral-classifier pair used non-referentially, as the predicate.

primaryText: Sono asa, komori-zawa-ni-wa, nana-hiki-no iwana-ga nobotte-ita. Jootaroo-zawa-ni-wa san-biki, ushiro-zawa-ni yon-hiki, koiwake-zawa-ni san-biki-ga ita.
translation: That morning, seven bull trout had appeared in Komori Lake. In Jotaro Lake there were three, in Ushiro Lake four, and in Koiwake Lake three.
comment: Classifier phrases introducing additional members of a category already introduced, pronouns of laziness.

primaryText: ... mae-ni futari suwattete sa, hitori-wa taaban-o maita indojin de sa, kore-ga unten shiteru. De, moo hitori-wa arabiajin da yo ne, futari-tomo ushiro-nanka minai-n da yo.
translation: ... there were two people sitting in the front seat. One was an Indian wearing a turban, and he was driving. The other one was an Arab, and neither of them looked back or anything.
comment: Naked numeral-classifier pairs singling out subsets of a grouping already introduced. The page prints no period after shiteru.

primaryText: Shuuichi-wa Shingo-no musuko da keredomo, Kikuko-ga kono-yoo-ni-shite-made Shuuichi-to musubarete inakereba naranai hodo, futari-wa risoo-no fuufu na-no ka, Shingo-wa utagai dasu to kagiri-ga nakatta.
translation: Even though Shuichi was his son, Shingo couldn't help wondering whether they were such an ideal couple that Kikuko should be linked to Shuichi to this extent.
comment: A numeral-classifier pair carrying the identity of individuals already mentioned, like a zero anaphor or pronoun, and at a distance excluding them. The page prints Shuichii in the translation.

primaryText: Mukashi-mukashi, soko-ni hitori-no ryooshi-ga arimashita.
translation: Long, long ago, there was a certain fisherman who lived there.
context: The beginning of a folk tale, after the island Kikaigashima has been introduced.
comment: 'One' plus classifier introduces a specific referent, like English 'a certain'; 'one' never appears in the anaphoric use, competing with zero anaphora and carrying little contrastive information.

primaryText: Yasuko-no imooto-no omokage-wa, futari-no kokoro-no soko-ni atta wake da.
translation: The image of Yasuko's younger sister remained in the heart of each of them.
context: Of the couple Yasuko and Shingo.
comment: The classifier phrase refers to the couple evenhandedly, avoiding the collective noun fuufu and the centring of Shingo-tachi or kanojo-tachi on one member.

primaryText: Ojisan-to, sono futari-no otoko-no ko-tachi-to kaeko-to kotatsu-ni atatte-imashita.
translation: (Our) uncle, his two sons, and Kaeko were warming themselves at the heated table.
comment: A classifier phrase and a plural suffix on one noun phrase without redundancy, against the hypothesis that classifiers and plural morphemes are in complementary distribution.

primaryText: Takai hana-to aoi iro-no me-o motta ningyoo-wa ichi-nichi-juu nazo-no yoona bishoo-o ukabete-iru.
translation: The mannequin, with its long nose and its blue eyes, smiled enigmatically all day long.
comment: Bare nouns are transnumeral: me 'eye' refers to two eyes and hana 'nose' to one.

primaryText: Sono ashi-ni-wa yubi-ga rop-pon aru.
translation: On that foot, there are six toes.
comment: A classifier phrase spells out the number of referents of a transnumeral noun.

primaryText: Ima, tookyoo-to-iu daitokai-ni iru kodomo-tachi-o mite-iru to, zuibun kawaisoo da to omou-no-wa ...
translation: What I find really sad when I see the children of the big city of Tokyo today is ...

alternatives.form: Ima, tookyoo-to iu daitokai-ni iru kodomo-o mite-iru to, zuibun kawaisoo da to omou no wa, ...

comment: A common noun with human referents takes a plural marker or not: Table 7.2, possible.

primaryText: Ima, tookyoo-to iu daitokai-ni iru neko-tachi-o mite-iru to, zuibun kawaisoo da to omou no wa, ...
translation: What I find really sad when I see the cats of the big city of Tokyo today is ...

alternatives.form: Ima, tookyoo-to iu daitokai-ni iru neko-o mite-iru to, zuibun kawaisoo da to omou no wa, ...

comment: A plural marker on a common noun with animal referents is marginal, acceptable only for personified animals: Table 7.2, rare. The page prints mite iru , in (7a); the frame is printed mite-iru to, in (6), (7b) and (8).

primaryText: Ima, tookyoo-to iu daitokai-ni aru tatemono-tachi-o mite-iru to, zuibun kawaisoo da to omou no wa, ...
translation: What I find really sad when I see the buildings of the big city of Tokyo today is ...

alternatives.form: Ima, tookyoo-to iu daitokai-ni aru tatemono-o mite-iru to, zuibun kawaisoo da to omou no wa, ...

comment: Common nouns with inanimate referents reject plural markers: Table 7.2, impossible.

primaryText: Kore-ra-no kao-no naka-ni-wa, ...
translation: Among these faces, ...
context: Fathers with children and youths with their lovers have gone in and out of the shop.
comment: With the same inanimate referents, the plural suffix is required on a demonstrative pronoun and unacceptable on a common noun, even one modified by a demonstrative.

primaryText: Kanja-wa hyakushoo-no okami-ya sono kodomo-ga ooi. Kare-ra-wa genkan-no agarikuchi-ni koshi-o oroshite ... matte-ita.
translation: The patients were primarily farmers' wives and children. They would wait, sitting in the entranceway, ...

alternatives.form: Kanja-tachi-wa hyakushoo-no okami-ya sono kodomo-ga ooi. Kare-ra-wa genkan-no agarikuchi-ni koshi-o oroshite ... matte-ita.
Kanja-wa hyakushoo-no okami-ya sono kodomo-ga ooi. Kare-wa genkan-no agarikuchi-ni koshi-o oroshite ... matte-ita.

comment: The common noun kanja may or may not carry the plural marker; the pronoun kare referring to the same group must.

primaryText: Endoo-san-tachi-to hanashi-o suru to, watashi-no gehinna bubun-ga hikidasarete-kuru-no.
translation: When I talk with Mr. Endo et al., my vulgar side comes out.
comment: On a proper noun the suffix is an associative plural, a group centred on Mr. Endo.

primaryText: Kodomo-tachi-ga shiken-o ukeru aida-ni okaasan-tachi-ga kono heya-de matsu yotei desu ga.
translation: The plan is for the mothers to wait in this room while the children take the test.
comment: On the common noun kodomo the suffix is a class plural only; okaasan, usable as a common noun or a proper name, yields a plural or an associative reading.

primaryText: Masutaa-to onaji-yoona katachi-no kitsune-no yoona kao-o motta otoko-ga iku-nin-mo suwatte-ita. ... kare-ra-no hosonagai zoo-no yoona me-wa ... Ano otoko-tachi-mo ima-wa doko-ka-de gasorin-sutando-no shujin-ni natte-iru kamoshirenai.
discourseSegments: Masutaa-to onaji-yoona katachi-no kitsune-no yoona kao-o motta otoko-ga iku-nin-mo suwatte-ita.
Watashi-tachi shinpei-o ijimeru toki, kare-ra-no hosonagai zoo-no yoona me-wa marude bishoo-demo shite-iru yoo datta.
Ano otoko-tachi-mo ima-wa doko-ka-de gasorin-sutando-no shujin-ni natte-iru kamoshirenai.
translation: Any number of men with fox-like faces like the (gas station) owner's were sitting (there). ... their beady little eyes seemed to be laughing. Those men too are probably gas station owners somewhere now.
comment: The referents are introduced by category with a classifier phrase and tracked as individuals with plural markers; the reverse order is unattested.

primaryText: neko-wa ne, kawaii kodomo-no toki dat-tara, go-rop-piki, kai-tai kedomo ...
translation: When cats are cute kittens, (I) feel like having five or six (of them), but ...
comment: A classifier phrase merely unitizes random members of a category, where a plural marker would flag particular tracking-worthy individuals.

primaryText: Iku-nin-mo-no onna-no kao-ga me-no mae-no kuukan-ni naranda. Sono onna-tachi-no naka-de-wa, watashi-no kodomo-o oroshita kao-mo majitte-ita.
discourseSegments: Iku-nin-mo-no onna-no kao-ga me-no mae-no kuukan-ni naranda.
Sono onna-tachi-no naka-de-wa, watashi-no kodomo-o oroshita kao-mo majitte-ita.
translation: The faces of a number of women lined up before (my) eyes. Among those women was the face (of one) who had aborted a child of mine.
comment: Introduction with noun plus classifier construction, then a noun plus plural marker: the typical pattern for groups of human referents.

primaryText: Mae-o hashitte-ita ni-dai-no jooyoosha-ga tsukamatta.
translation: The two cars ahead (of us) were caught.
comment: The pre-nominal construction is specific and exhaustive, 'the two cars'; the Q-Float variant reads 'two of the cars'.

primaryText: Ip-pon-no tabako-o sutte-mimashoo.
translation: Let's have a cigarette.
comment: The pre-nominal construction emphasises the referents as individuals and is awkward where distinctions between members are irrelevant; Q-Float is preferred.

primaryText: San-nin-no tomodachi-o matte-imasu.
translation: (I) am waiting for three friends.
context: The speaker has particular individuals in mind.
comment: Pre-nominal is preferred for particular individuals known to the speaker.

primaryText: Hisho-o san-nin sagashite-imasu.
translation: I am looking for three secretaries.
context: Any three secretaries will do; their identities are not known to the speaker.
comment: Q-Float is preferred where the individuals are not identifiable as individuals.

primaryText: Kare-ra futari-ga kita.
translation: The two of them came.
comment: The nominal of the pre-nominal construction must denote a category; a pronoun is possible only in the appositive construction.

primaryText: Sore-ga, atashi-tachi-no, otona-no hito-tsu-no tsutome demo-aru-n desu yo.
translation: That is one of our responsibilities as adults.
comment: 'One' plus classifier blocks the reading on which the referent exhausts the category.

primaryText: Taroo-tachi go-nin-ga haitte-kita.
translation: Taro et al., the five of them, came in.
comment: The appositive construction admits a proper name with the associative plural; the pre-nominal Go-nin-no Taroo-tachi-ga would mean five people all named Taro, (18).

primaryText: Haha-no nakunatta yoru, hitobito-no doojoo-wa, Kaeko hitori-ni atsumarimashita.
translation: The night that Mother died, everyone's sympathy fell on Kaeko alone.
comment: The appositive construction with a predictable number emphasises that the referent exhausts the group.

primaryText: Shiroi shinsatsuki-o kita oyaji, Asai joshu, kangofuchoo Toda, Suguro-no go-nin-ga byooshitsu-ni hairu to ...
translation: When the Old Man in (his) white examining gown, Assistant Asai, the head nurse, Toda, and Suguro, the five of them, entered the sickroom, ...
comment: The summative appositive: the nominal enumerates the individuals whose number the classifier phrase confirms.

primaryText: Enban-wa ichi-mai-zutsu tonde-iki, ...
translation: The disks flew one by one, ...
comment: The adverbial flavour of Q-Float shows in distributive uses.

primaryText: Kodomo-ga san-nin heya-ni haitte-kita.
translation: Three children came into the room.
comment: In introductions of individuated referents either construction may be used, with the same gloss.

primaryText: Kantoku-ga hitori-no onna-shashoo-to modotte-kita.
translation: The director returned with a conductress.
comment: Q-Float cannot quantify an argument bearing the comitative particle to.

primaryText: Kore-ra-no san-nin-no gakusei-ni furansu-go-ga wakarimasu.
translation: These three students understand French.
comment: The dative-marked subject of wakaru does not launch Q-Float, while its nominative-marked subject does, (34): evidence for a case-marking account over a grammatical-role account.

primaryText: Kore-ra-no gakusei-ga, san-nin furansu-go-ga wakarimasu.
translation: These three students understand French.
comment: The same subject with the nominative particle ga launches Q-Float.

primaryText: Otoko-ga kodomo-o san-nin yuukai shita.
translation: The/a man kidnapped three children.

readings.name: quantifies the transitive subject: three men

comment: A floated quantifier compatible with subject and object is preferentially construed with the object: the absolutive pattern of Q-Float.

primaryText: Hanako-ga fune-ga roku-soo boofuu-de shizunda to omotte-iru.
translation: Hanako thinks that six ships sank in the storm.

alternatives.form: Hanako-ga kodomo-ga roku-nin tylenol-ni seisankari-o ireta to omotte-iru.

comment: For some speakers Q-Float from an unaccusative subject is fine and from a transitive subject is not.

primaryText: Ta-ni, boku-no deshi-ga nan-nin-ka ite, ...
translation: In addition, a number of my students were there, ...
comment: Q-Float admits a partitive use, in which the quantity need not exhaust the group; the pre-nominal construction does not.

primaryText: kenjuu-o koshi-ni sageta heishi-ga ni-mei doa-o akete ikioiyoku tobi-orita. ... kogara-no futari-no heishi-tachi-no yoko-de kare-ra-no sei-ga amarini takai.
discourseSegments: kenjuu-o koshi-ni sageta heishi-ga ni-mei doa-o akete ikioiyoku tobi-orita.
kogara-no futari-no heishi-tachi-no yoko-de kare-ra-no sei-ga amarini takai.
translation: Two soldiers with pistols at their hips opened the door and energetically jumped down. ... They were exceedingly tall next to the two small soldiers.
comment: The referents are introduced with Q-Float, whose number information must be new, and re-mentioned with the exhaustive pre-nominal construction and a plural marker.

primaryText: Mai-nichi, mai-nichi, hito-tsu-no burausu-o kite, sooji-o shite-ita.
translation: Day after day (she) did the cleaning wearing the same blouse.

alternatives.form: Mai-nichi, mai-nichi, burausu hito-tsu-o kite, sooji-o shite-ita.
Mai-nichi, mai-nichi burausu-o hito-tsu kite, sooji-o shite-ita.

comment: The same phrase in the pre-nominal, appositive and Q-Float positions: the same blouse, only a blouse, and one blouse as new information.
